catalog_entry.label: Longest/shortest play, touchdown and field-goal extremes
catalog_entry.target: Probability that the maximum (or minimum) play length of a type over a window exceeds or falls below a yardage threshold.
catalog_entry.mechanism: League-wide extremes are produced by thinning a large count of eligible opportunities: snaps from the own 1-yard line for a 99-yard scrimmage play, and end-of-half or favourable-wind attempts at 68+ yards for a 70+ yard field goal. P(YES) is one minus exp(-rate times remaining games times conversion), where conversion is a tail probability (breakaway or kicker ceiling) that has few or no observed events, so exposure counts, a tail model and the running maximum to date are the inputs, not player season totals.

inputs.why: Baseline attempt and make model for 50+ and 60+ yard kicks by kicker, venue and weather; the starting point for the 70+ field goal factor.
The 70+ field goal contract needs a leg-ceiling estimate beyond observed makes; this is the make-probability factor of the expected count of 70+ makes.
The attempt-count factor for the 70+ field goal contract: with no attempts at 68+ yards the longest-FG market cannot move, so this isolates the decision stage from leg strength.
Exposure count for the 99+ yard contract: no snap from the own 1 means the market cannot resolve YES, so P(YES) is bounded by this rate.
Turns the exposure count into a probability of the one outcome the 99+ yard contract settles on; the tail extrapolation is the main uncertainty.
Provides the statistical backbone for both threshold contracts and the sanity check on the exposure-times-conversion decomposition.
Needed to price KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD readings under return-inclusive and scrimmage-only definitions.
Kicker accuracy by distance and kickoff touchback rate give the leg-power signal that feeds the ceiling tail.
Team and opponent rate of 40+ yard completions indicates how often deep shots from backed-up positions connect.
Per-carry explosive tail by rusher bounds how often a handoff from the own 1 can run the full field.
Yards-after-catch and air-yard split for receivers shows who can turn a short catch into a 99-yard score.
Counts snaps in the shadow of the own goal line, which is the exposure for the 99-yard play and for safeties.
Altitude and roof change effective kick distance (Denver adds range; domes remove wind), shifting 70+ make odds.
Wind speed and direction at kickoff vintages decide whether a 66-70 yard attempt is reachable.
Go-for-it versus kick policy by coach shapes how many long attempts are taken before the half-ending situation.
Holding and other flags nullify long plays under the rules text, converting a would-be 99-yard TD into no event.
Running maximum to date and the share of games remaining set the as-of state of both threshold contracts.
Kicker and quarterback availability changes the count of eligible long attempts over the remaining games.
Source agencies, regular-season scope and nullified-play exclusion define what counts for each strike.
Official settled value and timestamp for the max kick and max play, used to verify the record.
Official stat corrections to kick distance or yardage can flip a threshold market at the margin.

interactions.hypothesis: Expected 70+ makes equal attempts times make probability, so a strong-legged kicker on a coach who never attempts contributes almost nothing.
Altitude plus a strong tailwind adds several effective yards, converting a 66-yard ceiling kicker into a 70-yard threat only in that combined regime.
The 99-yard play probability is the product of the rare exposure count and a tiny conversion, so a rate uncertainty compounds multiplicatively.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNFLLONGESTFG-27-70 (floor_strike 70, greater_or_equal) resolves YES if the longest made field goal in the 2026-27 regular season is 70+ yards; only made kicks count and scope is the regular season by the quoted text. KXNFLLONGESTPLAY-27-99 (floor_strike 99) resolves YES if any play from scrimmage in the regular season gains at least 99 yards, on officially recorded stats of the Source Agencies, with penalty-nullified plays excluded. KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD have no market listed and no rules text, so their window, route inclusion and strike are unknown.

rules_evidence.quote: If the longest made field goal is 70+ yards in the 2026-27 Pro Football regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Settles on the season maximum of made kicks at or above 70 yards in the regular season only; a binary threshold on an order statistic.

rules_evidence.quote: If there is a play from scrimmage of at least 99 yards in the 2026-27 Pro Football regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Settles on a single play of 99 or more yards from scrimmage (not a return), any player, whole regular season.

rules_evidence.quote: therefore plays nullified by penalty are not considered for this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: A long play erased by a flag does not count, so penalty-nullification risk reduces the conversion probability.

variants_and_edge_cases: Series title for KXNFLLONGESTPLAY reads 'NFL Longest Touchdown' while the rules text says any play from scrimmage of 99+ yards; the two readings coincide only because a 99-yard gain from the own 1 ends in the end zone.

A scrimmage play cannot exceed 99 yards, so the 99+ strike is exactly 'a 99-yard play occurs' and requires a snap from the offence's own 1-yard line; kick and punt returns are not plays from scrimmage and do not count.

KXNFLLONGESTFG counts only made kicks; the kick-distance definition (spot of the kick versus line of scrimmage plus end-zone depth) is not in the sampled text, so the official recorded distance convention is assumed.

KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD are TITLE_ONLY: whether the window is a game or the season, whether return touchdowns count, and what the shortest-TD strike is are not visible; a 1-yard shortest TD is near-certain in any season.
Contract windows are the regular season only, so playoff and preseason kicks are outside scope; the market is partly already determined at any as-of date by the running maximum to date.
contract.settlement_data_source: Officially recorded stats of the Source Agencies (league play-by-play and gamebook); Kalshi names the league as Governing League. Post-game stat corrections are not described in the sampled rules.

mechanism.summary: League-wide extremes are generated by a small number of eligible opportunities passed through a rare conversion. For a 99-yard scrimmage play the opportunity is a snap from the offence's own 1-yard line (a punt downed at the 1, a goal-line stand turnover, or a penalty), and the conversion is a deep completion or run that no defender stops, with penalty nullification subtracting. For a 70+ yard field goal the opportunity is a late-half or late-game situation where a coach prefers a kick over a Hail Mary, and the conversion is a kicker with enough leg speed plus help from altitude, a dome or a tailwind. Both are thinned counts over about 272 games; probabilities are exp-type functions of the remaining game count, and the running maximum to date fixes the as-of state. Tail estimation, not bulk averages, is the problem.

stages.name: Opportunity creation: snaps and situations eligible for an extreme
stages.description: The league produces eligible snaps through special-teams field position (punts downed inside the 2, coffin-corner kicks), goal-line stands that turn the ball over on downs at the 1, and penalties that push an offence back. For kicks, eligible situations are 0-6 second end-of-half and end-of-game moments within about 68-75 yards of the goal line. The counts are small and unevenly spread over teams, and no player's skill creates them.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed counts, negative binomial per team-game; heavy clustering in a few games

stages.name: Decision: attempt a long kick or call a deep shot
stages.description: Given an eligible situation, the coach chooses between a long field goal, Hail Mary, kneel or punt, and from the own 1 chooses protection (safe runs, sneak) or play-action shots. Coach tendency, kicker's demonstrated range and timeouts determine the attempt; for the backed-up snap, offence scheme and QB deep-ball rate determine whether a deep shot is called rather than a safe run.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per situation with strong coach heterogeneity; near zero for most coaches

stages.name: Execution tail: breakaway or kick that reaches the threshold
stages.description: A 99-yard play needs an unblocked deep route, a miss by a deep safety or an untouched run, from a compressed field. A 70+ yard make needs ball speed and carry beyond any prior regular-season make, helped by altitude (reduced air density), roof and tailwind. The probability is a tail of a logistic or Pareto curve with very few historical points, so parameter uncertainty dominates the point estimate.
stages.distribution: Extreme-value tail with parameter uncertainty; orders of magnitude below bulk rates

stages.name: Nullification and aggregation over the remaining schedule
stages.description: A qualifying play or kick survives only if not erased by penalty (offensive holding on a long TD, a kick negated by a roughing flag then re-kicked) and then enters the league-wide maximum. Aggregation takes the running maximum to date, the count of remaining games and rest-of-season availability of kicker and QB, giving a Poisson-thinning probability of at least one qualifying event.
stages.distribution: Poisson-type with rate times remaining games; saturating in games left

stages.name: Settlement and record verification
stages.description: Settlement uses official recorded stats and the exact distance convention for kicks; contracts with no rules text (longest and shortest TD) depend on window and route inclusion. Stat corrections and source lag can alter the recorded length, and the market resolves from the record at season end.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the record; residual risk from corrections and ambiguity

nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.label: Own-one-yard-line snap rate (offence backed up at its own 1)
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.mechanism: A scrimmage play can gain at most 99 yards, and only when the snap is taken from the offence's own 1-yard line, so the count of such snaps is the exposure that a 99+ yard play is thinned out of.
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.rationale: Snaps from the 1 are produced by punts downed or fumbled at the 1, goal-line stands that end in a turnover on downs, and penalties walking the ball back; they are rare, clustered in a few team-games and not stable team traits. The contract is therefore a Poisson-thinning problem whose rate is this count, not any player's long-run yardage.
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.measurement: Per team-game, count snaps with yardline_100 = 99 (offence at own 1) from nflverse play-by-play, excluding kneels. Fit a negative-binomial rate on opponent-adjusted punting (inside-10 rate, net punt), defence goal-line stand rate and team penalty profile with 3-season pooling and shrinkage toward the league mean (about 30 team-games of prior weight). Output expected count for each remaining game; as-of = last completed game before the forecast.
nfl.own_one_yard_line_snap_rate.why: Exposure count for the 99+ yard contract: no snap from the own 1 means the market cannot resolve YES, so P(YES) is bounded by this rate.

nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.label: Backed-up breakaway conversion (P(99-yard TD | snap from own 1))
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.mechanism: Conditional probability that a snap taken from the own 1 becomes a full-field touchdown, produced by deep-pass completions behind a single-high or man-coverage defence or by an untouched run.
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.rationale: The defence is in a compressed field and often in short-yardage or goal-line personnel, which makes a defender-free deep route more plausible on play action, but any penalty (holding, intentional grounding in the end zone) or safety is far likelier than the breakaway. The league sample of true 99-yard plays is a handful in 60 seasons, so the rate must be extrapolated, not counted.
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.measurement: Estimate with a hierarchical logistic tail model on all snaps from yardline_100 >= 90 with outcome yards_gained >= 60, then extrapolate to >= 99 with a generalized Pareto tail anchored on the historical 99-yard plays and 80+ yard gains from deep starts; covariates: pass-rush pressure rate, QB deep-ball rate, defence two-high rate, offence tempo; 5-season window, half-life 2 seasons for scheme, shrinkage constant 25 deep-start snaps to the league mean.
free_sources: nflverse participation and FTN charting (free, limited seasons)
nfl.backed_up_breakaway_conversion.why: Turns the exposure count into a probability of the one outcome the 99+ yard contract settles on; the tail extrapolation is the main uncertainty.

nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.label: Kicker ceiling range tail (make probability at 66-75 yards)
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.mechanism: Per-kicker make probability beyond the demonstrated range, driven by leg speed, ball strike and launch angle, which pooled accuracy-by-distance tables cannot resolve.
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.rationale: Existing long-kick models cover 50+ and 60+ yard attempts, but a 70+ yard make sits beyond every observed regular-season make, so the question is who can plausibly reach it and how much wind, altitude and a dome shift the ceiling. Kickoff distance and touchback depth are an independent measure of leg power that is observable for every kicker.
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.measurement: Per kicker, fit a logistic make curve over kick distance using all attempts from 45 yards with a kicker-specific range term estimated from kickoff hang-adjusted distance (mean yards past the goal line on non-touchbacks, share of touchbacks into the back of the end zone) and career max make; shrink toward the position pool with 40 attempts of prior weight; adjust for roof, altitude and wind with the venue and weather inputs. Output P(make | attempt at 66, 68, 70, 72 yards, neutral and favourable conditions); as-of = last game before forecast.
nfl.kicker_ceiling_range_tail.why: The 70+ field goal contract needs a leg-ceiling estimate beyond observed makes; this is the make-probability factor of the expected count of 70+ makes.

nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.label: Long field-goal attempt hazard at end of half and game
nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.mechanism: Number of snaps per season where the clock and score make a 65+ yard attempt the best option over a Hail Mary or punt, set by coach choice, timeouts and the kicker's stated range.
nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.rationale: A 70+ attempt almost never occurs in normal play because a punt wins field position; it occurs with 0-5 seconds left in a half or game when only a kick keeps points alive. Whether a coach sends the kicker for 68 or throws a Hail Mary is a policy that varies by coach and by whether the kicker has shown the range.
nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.measurement: From play-by-play, count snaps with kick_distance >= 60 or qualifying situations (game_seconds_remaining in half <= 6, offence between own 40 and opponent 50, trailing by <= 3 or tied at the half) and estimate P(attempt | situation) by head coach with a hierarchical logit (coach, kicker max make, wind, roof, timeouts). 4-season window; shrink coach rates toward the league with 15 qualifying situations of prior weight. Output expected 65+, 68+, 70+ yard attempts for the remaining schedule.
free_sources: nflverse play_by_play (qtr, game_seconds_remaining, timeout counts, kick_distance)
NFL gamebook text for coach statements (free, scrape)
nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard.why: The attempt-count factor for the 70+ field goal contract: with no attempts at 68+ yards the longest-FG market cannot move, so this isolates the decision stage from leg strength.

nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.label: Extreme-value tail fit for play length (long plays and long kicks)
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.mechanism: Generalized Pareto or Gumbel-type fit to the upper tail of scrimmage-play and kick lengths, giving return levels for the league-wide season maximum.
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.rationale: The contract is a threshold on a maximum, so only the extreme tail matters. A bulk model (mean yards per play) is nearly irrelevant, and the cap of 99 yards plus the finite number of own-goal-line snaps means a bounded-tail fit with exposure weighting is required. Few historical points mean parameter uncertainty must be carried into the probability.
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.measurement: Using all regular-season plays since 1999, fit a peaks-over-threshold model (threshold 60 yards for plays, 56 yards for kick distance) with Poisson exceedance rate per 1,000 snaps by start-yardline bucket; propagate parameter uncertainty by posterior or bootstrap; produce return-level probabilities P(max >= 99) and P(max kick >= 70) for N remaining games, and the running maximum to date as the as-of state.
free_sources: Pro-Football-Reference longest-play and longest-FG record lists (free, scrape)
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.why: Provides the statistical backbone for both threshold contracts and the sanity check on the exposure-times-conversion decomposition.

nfl.td_play_length_by_source.label: Touchdown play length by source (scrimmage, interception, fumble, kick and punt return, missed-FG return)
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.mechanism: Distribution of touchdown lengths split by scoring route, because returns can exceed 99 yards and short touchdowns come from goal-line runs and sneaks.
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.rationale: Longest-TD and shortest-TD contracts have no rules text, so which routes count is unknown. A longest-TD maximum can reach 100-109 yards only on a return, whereas the scrimmage maximum is 99; the shortest TD is 1 yard in effectively every season, making it near-certain unless the strike is defined otherwise.
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.measurement: Tabulate touchdown length by scoring route from play-by-play for 1999-2026 (yards_gained for scrimmage; return_yards for returns; kick-return TDs measured from the catch spot), with counts per season, the per-season maximum and minimum, and per-route rate per 1,000 snaps with the same tail model as above; record both with and without return TDs so that either contract reading can be priced.
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.why: Needed to price KXNFLLONGESTTD and KXNFLSHORTESTTD readings under return-inclusive and scrimmage-only definitions.

nfl.long_fg_attempt_and_make_model.reason: Closest existing model for the 70+ field goal series, but stops at 50+ and 60+ and cannot extrapolate beyond the demonstrated range alone.

nfl.kicker.reason: Accuracy by distance and touchback rate give leg-power evidence, but accuracy under 55 yards is not the quantity that decides a 70-yard make.

nfl.long_completion_tail_rate.reason: 20+ and 40+ yard rates describe the bulk of the long tail; the 99-yard event is far beyond it and needs the own-1 start conditioning.

nfl.rush_yardage_tail.reason: Explosive-run tail by rusher informs one of two ways a scrimmage play can go 99, but runs rarely start at the own 1 in open space.

nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.reason: Includes longest-play probability by receiver, useful for who completes a deep shot; the player-level frame misses the exposure count.

nfl.endzone_exposure_plays.reason: Counts end-zone area snaps; related to the own-1 exposure but defined by the end zone, not exactly the 1-yard line.

nfl.venue.reason: Altitude and roof directly change kick range; irrelevant for scrimmage plays beyond surface speed.

nfl.weather_pit.reason: Wind at kickoff vintages decides whether a 66-70 yard kick is reachable; secondary for the scrimmage contract.

nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate.reason: Mid-field fourth-down policy is adjacent to, but weaker than, the end-of-half attempt policy that actually yields 68+ yard kicks.

nfl.penalties.reason: Rules text excludes nullified plays, so flag rate on long gains is a real subtractive factor but a modest one.

nfl.season_to_date_pace.reason: The as-of state is the running maximum and games left, not a per-player pace; keep only for the remaining-exposure computation.

nfl.games_played_dist.reason: Only matters through kicker and QB availability; the extremes are league-wide so one absence rarely moves the probability.

m.rules_text.reason: Rules define regular-season scope, the 99-yard play definition and the penalty exclusion; two series have text and two do not.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Settled values and timestamps verify the record but add no forecasting signal.

m.stat_correction_risk.reason: Corrections to yardage or kick distance could change a threshold outcome and the rules name official stats as the source.

interactions.mechanism: Expected number of 70+ makes is attempts at that range times make probability, so either factor near zero keeps the sum near zero; a strong-legged kicker on a coach who prefers a Hail Mary adds almost nothing, and a coach willing to try with a kicker below range adds only misses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute expected 70+ makes per team as the product of the two factors and compare with a model that sums them; check that the product model ranks past 64+ yard attempts better.

interactions.mechanism: Altitude (reduced air density) plus a strong following wind adds several effective yards; a kicker with a 66-yard ceiling reaches 70 only when both help, a regime that exists in a few venues and weeks and in domes only for the altitude-free case.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate make probability at 62+ yards with a venue-by-wind interaction term and test the slope above 15 mph tailwind versus roof or sea-level venues.

interactions.mechanism: The 99-yard play is Poisson thinning: exposure count times conversion; uncertainty in the count and the tail compounds, and snaps cluster by team and week, so the joint distribution is wider than independent factors imply.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate remaining games with a negative binomial exposure and a Beta conversion, and compare predictive intervals with a product-of-point-estimates calculation on historical seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Long plays from deep starts carry a high chance of a holding flag or a rarer illegal block, which the rules exclude; the nullification share is conditional on play length and the offence's penalty profile, so it lowers the conversion more for teams that hold often.
interactions.how_to_test: From historical 50+ yard gains, estimate the nullification rate by length bucket and team penalty rate, then test whether it rises with yards gained.

interactions.mechanism: Once games are played without an event, remaining exposure shrinks, so the probability of YES decays toward zero in the last weeks, while any past event resolves it; the response of P(YES) to games left is exponential not linear.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest the hazard decay on prior seasons conditioned on no event before week N, comparing a constant-rate model with the thinned count.

nonlinearities.shape: Steep logistic collapse of make probability beyond about 63-65 yards
nonlinearities.why: Make probability falls from near 40 percent at 60 yards to a small tail past 66, so a few yards of kicker or wind help changes the 70+ probability by multiples, not by an additive amount.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold with saturation in tailwind speed; zero effect in domes
nonlinearities.why: Wind adds distance only after it exceeds roughly 10-15 mph and its effect is capped by the kick trajectory; roof games get zero tailwind benefit, so the response is piecewise, not linear.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating exponent: P(at least one) = 1 - exp(-rate x games)
nonlinearities.why: The contract settles on at least one event, so the probability saturates as the expected count grows and is nearly linear only when the count is small.

catalog_entry.label: NFL Draft and Supplemental Draft selection markets
contract_types: Draft pick slot (1st overall, exact selection)
Team draft by position or round
catalog_entry.target: Probability a named prospect is selected at a slot, range or positional order, or a team makes/uses a given pick, per the official Draft results.
catalog_entry.mechanism: Draft outcomes come from a deterministic order process (season results, tiebreakers and trades decide who holds each slot) combined with team decisions among prospects: each team picks from a board shaped by consensus value, positional need, quarterback regime and decision-maker habits, subject to the prospect declaring and passing medicals. Trades before and on draft night break the order, and positional order statistics (3rd quarterback taken, top five) are correlated across prospects, so a joint slot simulation is required.

inputs.why: Consensus rankings, draft order and team needs are the baseline of every draft selection contract.
Race for the worst record and strength-of-schedule tiebreak decides who holds the first pick and the order of the top slots.
QB-class order, team need and trade-up model feed quarterback-order contracts.
KXNFLDRAFTSELECT settles on the team making the 32nd overall pick, which is the Super Bowl winner under these rules unless the pick was traded; slot 1 is set by the worst record.
Resolves the team-level contract rule that a traded pick resolves to the team that actually selects, and drives pick-slot markets for named prospects.
Converts a ranking into the probabilities that top-5, exact-slot, over/under and Nth-at-position contracts actually settle on.
Drives which position a pick holder drafts: the main team-side term in position-drafted, team-draft-by-position and QB-order contracts.
Every named-prospect contract carries the pre-condition that the player is in the pool; the hurdle is largest in the months before the declaration deadline.
The position and trade behavior of the picking team is the part that a consensus ranking cannot supply.
Settlement of the QB-order and position-drafted series depends on which source's label counts for hybrid players.
Needed for KXNFLSDRAFTTOP, a separate mechanism from the April draft that no consensus board models.
Season simulation distribution supplies the uncertainty in final standings that sets slots and the 31st and 32nd picks.
Standings simulation with tiebreakers gives each team's probability of finishing at the bottom or winning the title.
Timestamped reporting about team intentions, prospect visits and medical updates moves the pick distribution.
Cap room and contract guarantees decide whether a team can afford a rookie slot or a veteran QB.
Roster turnover and returning production indicate positional holes and need.
A coaching or GM change resets draft philosophy and quarterback need.
Draft-capital prior for unproven quarterbacks measures how a team views an incumbent against a rookie.
Conversion of insider draft reports into official picks shows how reliable pre-draft leaks are.
Calendar of the combine, declaration deadline and draft night structures when information arrives.
Reference-class frequencies for off-field outcomes provide priors where there is no specific board data.
Wording on traded picks, positions and which draft counts defines settlement for each series.

mechanism.summary: A draft selection outcome is generated by a chain: season results and tiebreakers fix the order of picks, trades reassign who holds slots before and on draft night, prospects must declare and clear medical gates, and each pick-holder chooses from a board that mixes consensus value, positional need, quarterback regime and the decision-makers' habits. Ordinal contracts (3rd quarterback taken, top five, over/under a slot) are order statistics over correlated choices, so one team's decision at pick 2 changes every later probability. Consensus rank gives the centre of the distribution, but position premiums and trade-ups produce skewed, heavy-tailed slot errors, so the unit of analysis is a joint simulation of the whole first round rather than separate per-player estimates.

stages.name: Eligibility and gating: who is in the pool
stages.description: A prospect must declare for the draft, be eligible and pass medical and character checks before any team can select him. In November the college season is underway, declaration is months away, and in-season injuries change value; for named-prospect contracts this is a precondition, and for the Supplemental Draft eligibility is a league ruling on a petition.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per prospect with a strong prior by projected round; late shocks from injury

stages.name: Order formation: standings and tiebreakers to slots
stages.description: Final standings and playoff results are mapped to slots by the league's rules: the worst record picks first (strength-of-schedule tiebreak), playoff teams are placed by round exited, and the Super Bowl loser and winner take 31 and 32. The order is not known in November, so each team's slot is a distribution from a season simulation, and forfeited picks can shift overall numbering.
stages.distribution: Discrete slot distribution with fat tails for playoff teams; exact once the season ends

stages.name: Team choice: boards, need, quarterback regime and decision-maker habits
stages.description: Each pick-holder selects from its board. Consensus value sets the initial ordering, positional need and the quarterback regime tilt choices (a holder with no franchise QB near the top of the class faces strong pressure), and GM and coach habits determine reach tendency, trade-down frequency and how positions like EDGE are valued.
stages.distribution: Categorical choice among a few candidates with team-specific heterogeneity

stages.name: Trades and reshuffling before and on draft night
stages.description: Teams trade up for a quarterback or a rare talent and trade down for assets; each trade changes the team that makes a given pick and the demand curve for later slots. Trade-up hazard depends on the consensus gap between the prospect and the next, the buyer's pick stock and need, and the seller's willingness, and it is partly reported by insiders ahead of time.
stages.distribution: Rare but high-impact jumps; conditional on gap and need

stages.name: Realization, labelling and settlement
stages.description: Selections are announced on draft night and settle from the official record: slot, team, and the position label given by the league. Hybrid labels (edge versus linebacker) and Nth-at-position rules depend on that label; markets close at the draft, so information vintage must stop before the first selection.
stages.distribution: Deterministic after the draft; label disagreement risk at position boundaries

nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.label: Draft order rules engine (season result to overall slot)
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.mechanism: Deterministic mapping from final standings, playoff results and tiebreakers to overall slots 1-32 of round one, including the champion at 32, the Super Bowl loser at 31 and forfeited or traded slots.
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.rationale: Slot ownership before the draft is not a model output but a rules calculation on results that are still uncertain in November: non-playoff teams are ordered by record then strength of schedule, playoff teams by round exited, so the 32nd pick equals the Super Bowl winner. Forfeitures can shorten a round and shift overall numbering.
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.measurement: Implement league draft-order rules: non-playoff teams ascending by win percentage, ties broken by strength of schedule then divisional and conference tiebreakers; picks 19-24 wild card losers, 25-28 divisional losers, 29-30 conference-final losers, 31 Super Bowl loser, 32 champion; apply the league's list of forfeited picks. Run on simulated seasons from the season simulation to give the slot distribution per team; as-of = latest game result and the official pick-transaction list.
nfl.draft_order_rules_engine.why: KXNFLDRAFTSELECT settles on the team making the 32nd overall pick, which is the Super Bowl winner under these rules unless the pick was traded; slot 1 is set by the worst record.

nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.label: Draft pick ownership and trade graph (who holds each slot, trade-up hazard)
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.mechanism: Current owner of each first-round pick, the set of future-pick bundles, and the chance a slot changes hands before or on draft night.
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.rationale: Contracts settle on the team that ultimately makes the pick and on pick-order outcomes, so ownership at the moment of selection is the relevant variable. Trade-ups for a quarterback, by a team that holds a later pick, are the main way that consensus order is broken, and there is a documented pre-draft window when picks are exchanged.
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.measurement: Maintain a table of pick-by-pick ownership with transaction timestamps; estimate P(slot k traded before selection) with a logistic on slot, consensus gap between the top prospects, holder's quarterback need and asset stock (picks held), using the last 15 drafts for the top 10 slots with shrinkage toward the draft-wide average of about 30 percent for picks 1-10; as-of = the latest official trade list.
free_sources: Over The Cap / Spotrac pick ownership (free_limited)
nfl.draft_pick_ownership_trade_graph.why: Resolves the team-level contract rule that a traded pick resolves to the team that actually selects, and drives pick-slot markets for named prospects.

nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.label: Prospect slot dispersion model (consensus rank to realized pick distribution)
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.mechanism: Empirical distribution of realized pick minus consensus rank by rank band and position, giving heavy-tailed, skewed slot distributions that vary by position premium.
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.rationale: Consensus boards give a central ranking, but markets ask for ordinal events (1st overall, top 5, before pick N, 3rd quarterback). The spread of realized slot around consensus grows with rank, is asymmetric for quarterbacks (they are taken early) and depends on how close the point-in-time board was to the draft.
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.measurement: From 2010-2026 drafts, join point-in-time consensus rank (mean of public boards, dated 90, 30 and 1 days before the draft) to realized pick; fit a quantile or ordinal regression of pick on rank, position and days-to-draft, with a position premium for QB and EDGE and a spread that rises with rank; produce a full slot pmf per prospect and a cross-prospect order-statistic simulation preserving ordering constraints. Shrink thin positions toward the pooled model with 20 draftees of prior weight.
free_sources: NFL Mock Draft Database (free, scrape; historical vintage needs own capture)
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.why: Converts a ranking into the probabilities that top-5, exact-slot, over/under and Nth-at-position contracts actually settle on.

nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.label: Team positional need and quarterback regime (who needs what at their slot)
nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.mechanism: A per-team, per-position need score from starters' age, contract end, production and offseason moves, plus a quarterback state (franchise QB, bridge, none, draft-and-develop).
nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.rationale: Slot buyers choose among a handful of boards; need breaks ties between near-equal prospects and sets quarterback pressure: a top-3 holder without a franchise QB faces a qualitatively different incentive than a holder with a long-term deal. Free agency and trades before the draft shift need so a stale vintage is wrong.
nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.measurement: Score need per team-position as a weighted sum of (starter age above position median, contract years remaining below 2, last-season EPA or PFF-style grade percentile, depth chart gap after free agency); QB regime coded from contract guarantees, recent draft capital and benching history. Refresh weekly until the draft; as-of = last transaction timestamp; shrink by position-group priors with 10 team-years constant.
free_sources: nflverse rosters, depth charts and contracts (free)
raw_data: roster and depth chart by position
nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.why: Drives which position a pick holder drafts: the main team-side term in position-drafted, team-draft-by-position and QB-order contracts.

nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.label: Prospect declaration, eligibility and medical status
nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.mechanism: Whether a named prospect enters the draft pool at all, remains draft-eligible, and passes medicals, testing and character gates before the draft.
nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.rationale: A named-prospect contract resolves NO if the player returns to college, is ruled ineligible or falls to a medical and disciplinary red flag. In November the declaration is still months away, the NCAA season is in progress and injuries during the college season change draft value; the deadline for underclassmen is known but the choices are not.
nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.measurement: Estimate P(declare) per prospect by class, projected round (first-round projected prospects declare at about 95 percent, others far less), return-to-school incentives and injury status; add a medical flag risk (injury and surgery history) and combine/pro-day measurement update after the testing window. Use the 5 most recent draft classes as the base rate; as-of = last official early-entry list or the player's statement timestamp.
nfl.prospect_declaration_eligibility_med.why: Every named-prospect contract carries the pre-condition that the player is in the pool; the hurdle is largest in the months before the declaration deadline.

nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.label: General manager and head coach draft behavior history
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.mechanism: Per decision-maker record of trading down, trading up for quarterbacks, positional reaches versus consensus, and tenure resets when GM or coach changes.
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.rationale: The picks are made by a small number of people with persistent habits: some GMs trade down 40 percent of the time, others take the best available; a new GM or coach resets need and scheme (4-3 versus 3-4 edge definition). Reaches above consensus rank are a stable personal trait.
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.measurement: For each GM and head coach, compute (a) trade-down and trade-up frequency in rounds 1-2, (b) mean reach versus consensus rank by position, (c) positions drafted in round one, using their past 5 drafts with tenure weighting and shrinkage to the league mean with 3 drafts of prior weight; flag new decision makers and set a new-regime weight to the franchise's last regime at 50 percent.
nfl.gm_draft_behavior_history.why: The position and trade behavior of the picking team is the part that a consensus ranking cannot supply.

nfl.draft_position_label_governance.label: Draft position label governance (official position classification)
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.mechanism: Mapping from a prospect to the position label that settles contracts (QB, RB, WR, TE, OL, DL, EDGE, LB, DB), including how the governing league and source agencies label hybrid players.
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.rationale: Position-drafted and Nth-at-position contracts depend on labels, and the rules text states that if positions differ across source agencies the Governing League's position is used. Edge rushers, hybrid linebackers and safeties-cornerbacks and tackle-guard swaps are exactly where labels diverge.
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.measurement: Build a label table from the league's draft tracker position at the time of selection and compare with the college and consensus-board labels for the last 10 classes; compute the disagreement rate by position pair (EDGE versus DL versus LB, S versus CB, OT versus OG) and carry it as probability mass into Nth-at-position markets; as-of = each pick announcement.
nfl.draft_position_label_governance.why: Settlement of the QB-order and position-drafted series depends on which source's label counts for hybrid players.

nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.label: Supplemental Draft mechanics (eligibility, weighted order, bid cost)
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.mechanism: Supplemental Draft eligibility via petition, a weighted-lottery order based on previous season records, and the bid rule that costs a team its same-round pick in the next regular draft.
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.rationale: This draft is held rarely and picks only the few players the league declares eligible; whether a named player is selected depends on whether any team will pay a future pick, so the key variables are eligibility ruling, the player's expected round and team needs, not consensus board ranking.
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.measurement: Count Supplemental Draft years with and without picks over 1977-2026 for a base rate; model P(selected) per eligible player from projected round (a bid costs the same-round pick next year, so teams bid only if the player is worth it), team round-pick inventory, and the league ruling date; as-of = league announcement of eligibility and the date of the draft.
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.why: Needed for KXNFLSDRAFTTOP, a separate mechanism from the April draft that no consensus board models.

interactions.mechanism: A quarterback-needy team that holds a later pick trades up only when the gap to the top quarterback is large and it holds enough assets, so need raises a quarterback's expected slot only through the trade graph; with a top-3 pick and no quarterback the effect is direct.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realized quarterback slots in drafts split by need of the top-5 holders and by presence of a trade-up; test the need effect with and without a trade indicator.

interactions.mechanism: Quarterbacks are drafted earlier than consensus rank and the order among them is correlated: if the first quarterback goes first overall the remaining quarterbacks' slots shift together, so the 3rd-quarterback contract is an order statistic of dependent slots.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the class with and without a position premium and rank-order correlation and compare with realized orders of quarterbacks in 2010-2026 drafts.

interactions.mechanism: The 32nd pick is the Super Bowl winner and the 1st pick the worst record, so the slot distribution is the extremes of a simulated season: tails dominate and teams that look similar by rating have very different probabilities of the end slots.
interactions.how_to_test: Run the season simulation through the rules engine and compare predicted end-slot distributions with historical pre-playoff projections.

interactions.mechanism: Prospects projected in round one declare almost surely, so declaration risk is a threshold in projected round; below the threshold return-to-school and medical flags dominate and the slot distribution is a mixture with a mass at undrafted.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit P(declare) against consensus rank at the declaration deadline and test for a step near the first-round boundary.

interactions.mechanism: Team need only converts to a pick when the decision-maker's habit permits it: a GM who rarely reaches ignores need for the best player, while a reach-prone GM acts on need, so the two multiply rather than add.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress the position drafted on need by GM reach propensity and test the interaction coefficient.

nonlinearities.shape: Dispersion widens roughly linearly with consensus rank and is right-skewed for positions with a premium
nonlinearities.why: The standard deviation of realized pick around consensus is small for the top prospects and large later, so probabilities for top-5 and exact-slot events fall sharply with the rank, unlike over/under events near the middle.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic step: quarterback selection probability jumps once need exceeds a no-franchise-QB threshold
nonlinearities.why: A holder with a franchise QB almost never takes one in round one while a holder without one near the top does with high probability, so the response is a step, not a linear need effect.

nonlinearities.shape: Trade probability rises convexly with the consensus gap between the first and second prospects at a slot
nonlinearities.why: When one prospect is clearly above the rest, buyers pay to move; when prospects are equal, the pick holder keeps the slot, so trade risk is convex in the gap.

catalog_entry.label: Super Bowl MVP and its position/defense/non-QB variants
catalog_entry.target: Probability a player (or position group) is named Super Bowl MVP, given the game outcome and in-game performance.
catalog_entry.mechanism: The award is a one-game vote that mostly goes to a member of the winning team, so P(player) is the product of the chance his team reaches and wins the final and the chance that, given a win, panel and fans credit him for the highlight lines the box score contains. Quarterbacks have a premium, but a non-QB or defender wins when the game script favours the run, defence or a scoring play; so the inputs are team-level path and matchup, game-level credit allocation and the voting mechanics, not a season stat total.

inputs.why: Sets the team-level probability that the winning side contains a given player, the first factor of every Super Bowl MVP variant.
Gives the second factor for each variant (overall, defensive, non-QB, position) once the winning team is fixed.
Base rate for the position and non-QB contracts, which have no season-stat process: it sets the prior that the game-level model refines.
Drives the defensive-player Super Bowl MVP variant, which is the only one of the four contracts decided mainly by defence.
Distribution of conference champions and finalists from the season simulation sets who reaches the game.
Seed, bye and path difficulty change the chance each team reaches the final.
Full-strength rating applies in the final because injured starters return or are lost across the two weeks.
Market-free opponent-adjusted rating feeds the matchup win probability.
Starting QB status is decisive: a backup or injured QB moves MVP mass from QB to other positions.
Vintaged injury reports before the game update candidate availability and team win probability.
Regressed QB efficiency gives the prior that the QB posts the highlight line.
Vote-share model maps in-game lines to selection probability; adapted to the panel.
Panel composition, timing and tie rules determine how credit becomes a winner.
Look-alike teammates split credit and lower each one's selection chance.
Single-game ceiling tails give the chance of outlier stat lines in the game that decide the vote.
Anytime and multi-TD scoring rates by role project who scores in the game.
Game-script lattice indicates pass-heavy or run-heavy games and defensive control, shifting credit by unit.
Defensive and special-teams TD hazard sets the chance a defender or returner wins.
Pass-rush matchup quality raises the sack opportunity for edge defenders.
Neutral venue roof and surface affect passing versus running, a small shift in who posts the line.
Playoff overtime rule adds snaps and tail stat lines, boosting QB credit in extra-time games.
Narrative and injury reports in the two-week window affect candidacy and roles.
Award definition, eligibility and tie rules; no series has sampled rules text.
Official MVP announcement and position classification verify settlement.

interactions.hypothesis: P(player MVP) is the product of his team's win probability and his conditional credit share, so a star on a likely loser can be below a role player on the favourite.
Defender MVP mass rises in low-scoring, turnover-driven wins where a pick-six or multi-sack game becomes the standout line.
A compromised or backup QB moves the position prior from quarterback to RB, WR and defence, so the base-rate shift is conditional on QB status.

contract.settlement_definition: All four series (overall, defensive player, position of the winner, non-QB) are TITLE_ONLY with no market listed and no rules text sampled, so nothing about settlement is verified. By the contract titles the outcome is the official Super Bowl MVP named by the league (a panel and fan vote), and the variants restrict the winner to a defensive player, report the position, or exclude quarterbacks. Overtime, co-MVP, an MVP from the losing team, postponed game and classification of special-teams players are not stated in any sampled text.
variants_and_edge_cases: KXNFLSBMVP, KXNFLSBMVPDEF, KXNFLSBMVPPOS and KXNFLSBMVPQB are all TITLE_ONLY: no rules were sampled, so co-winner handling, losing-team winners and tie rules are unknown (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS).
The defensive variant must define whether a special-teams returner or kicker counts as defensive; historical winners include a returner and defenders, so classification affects the YES set.
The position variant resolves on the position label of the winner; labels for hybrids (a running back who lines up as a receiver) depend on the official source and are not given.
The non-QB variant is the complement of the QB outcome among all winners; a co-MVP of a QB and a non-QB would split the interpretation unless the rules say otherwise.
The game is a single event; a postponement, cancellation or overtime changes the sample of snaps from which the box-score highlights are drawn, but overtime handling by the voters is not stated.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not stated: the announced Super Bowl MVP by the league is the presumed source of truth. No rules text sampled.

mechanism.summary: A Super Bowl MVP outcome factors into three layers. First, team layer: which two teams reach the game (conference path and seeding) and who wins at a neutral site after two weeks, using full-strength lineups. Second, game layer: given a win, the in-game script and box score decide which player posts a standout line (a passing line with multiple touchdowns, a large rushing or receiving game, several sacks, a defensive or return touchdown), which depends on who is available and the matchup. Third, voting layer: a media panel and a fan vote convert highlights into a name, with a quarterback premium, split credit among teammates and decisions made late in the game. Position and non-QB variants are aggregations of the same chain over player sets.

stages.name: Team path: which teams reach the Super Bowl
stages.description: Each conference champion emerges from a bracket after seeding, byes and matchups; the weeks before the final shift each team's chance to reach it. The set of finalists is uncertain in November and is a draw from a season simulation with playoff structure, not a ranking.
stages.distribution: Discrete finalist-pair distribution from simulation; heavy mass on top seeds

stages.name: Final: neutral-site winner at full strength
stages.description: The finalists play at a neutral site after a two-week gap, with no home advantage, a playoff overtime rule and lineups that change with injury returns and losses. The winner's identity is a close-to-coin-flip draw modified by the margin SD, so the favourite's win rate is modest even with a rating edge.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli with win probability typically 35-65 percent; margin SD near 13 points

stages.name: Game script: who dominates the winner's game
stages.description: Conditional on the winner, the game shape (high scoring through the air, controlled run game, defensive turnovers, special-teams score) determines which unit posts the visible line; pace, pass rate and late-lead behavior matter, and overtime adds snaps.
stages.distribution: Mixture over script regimes with correlated player lines

stages.name: Player lines and credit allocation among the winner's players
stages.description: Given a script, the winner's players post lines: passing yards and TDs for a quarterback, yards and scores for receivers and backs, sacks and takeaways for defenders. Credit is shared when two teammates post strong lines, so top-line outliers drive the winner and teammate splits lower each player's probability.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed single-game lines; credit is a softmax over correlated candidates

stages.name: Voting and announcement
stages.description: A media panel and a fan vote name the MVP, with the choice formed during the late part of the game; quarterbacks are favoured, narratives (a comeback, a record) matter, and a co-MVP or losing-team winner is rare but possible. Panel composition and timing are the voting mechanics; contract variants then filter the winner by position or unit.
stages.distribution: Categorical outcome with QB premium and rare exceptions; position markets are aggregations

nfl.sb_neutral_site_matchup_win_prob.label: Super Bowl neutral-site matchup win probability (market-free)
nfl.sb_neutral_site_matchup_win_prob.mechanism: Win probability for each possible pair of conference champions at a neutral site after a two-week break, from full-strength lineups and the playoff overtime rule, then weighted by the chance each pair meets.
nfl.sb_neutral_site_matchup_win_prob.rationale: MVP probability for a player is P(his team reaches the game) times P(wins) times P(he is chosen given a win), so the first two factors are team-level quantities fixed by path and matchup. The full-strength rating, not the season average, applies because injured starters return or are lost in the two weeks and home advantage is absent.
nfl.sb_neutral_site_matchup_win_prob.measurement: Combine the own opponent-adjusted team rating with a full-strength lineup adjustment (starter availability at kickoff minus 2 weeks), zero home-field advantage, and a rest adjustment for bye weeks (about +0.5 points for a bye-week team in the semifinal only); convert margin to win probability with the single-game SD of about 13 points; sum over simulated conference-championship pairs from the season simulation. As-of = latest game result and injury vintage; shrink ratings toward the league mean using 10 games of prior weight.
nfl.sb_neutral_site_matchup_win_prob.why: Sets the team-level probability that the winning side contains a given player, the first factor of every Super Bowl MVP variant.

nfl.sb_mvp_winner_conditional_credit.label: Winning-team credit allocation (P(MVP | team wins) by player and unit)
nfl.sb_mvp_winner_conditional_credit.mechanism: Model of how credit divides among the winner's players: quarterback line, receivers, running backs, pass rushers, defensive scorers and returners, given the game script that leads to a win.
nfl.sb_mvp_winner_conditional_credit.rationale: Voters pick from the winning team (a single non-winner exception exists), so what matters is which unit posts the visible highlights. A high-passing quarterback line, a defensive touchdown or a decisive turnover can overrule season reputation; the mechanism is a function of in-game box score not season stats, so season-stat awards inputs are weak here.
nfl.sb_mvp_winner_conditional_credit.measurement: Fit a multinomial or conditional logit on all Super Bowls since 1967 (and playoff winners as extra data) with player-level covariates measured in the game: passing yards, passing TDs, rush and receiving yards, total TDs, defensive TDs and takeaways, sacks, game-winning play indicator, position dummy; add a QB-premium intercept shrunk with a hierarchical prior; predict on simulated game box scores from the winner's player projection (use the single-game ceiling and TD rate inputs). Output P(player MVP | team wins) and position-level aggregates.
free_sources: Pro-Football-Reference Super Bowl box scores and MVP list (free, scrape)
raw_data: Super Bowl box scores by player
nfl.sb_mvp_winner_conditional_credit.why: Gives the second factor for each variant (overall, defensive, non-QB, position) once the winning team is fixed.

nfl.sb_mvp_historical_position_base_rate.label: Super Bowl MVP historical base rates by position, team result and era
nfl.sb_mvp_historical_position_base_rate.mechanism: Long-run shares of the award by position (QB, RB, WR, defence, special teams), incidence of losing-team and co-winners, and drift by era.
nfl.sb_mvp_historical_position_base_rate.rationale: With about 60 events the position shares are the only data for position and non-QB contracts, so they must be handled as shrinkage priors rather than hard frequencies; the quarterback share, the mix of defensive winners and cases of unusual winners (a returner, a losing-team defender, co-MVPs) shape tails.
nfl.sb_mvp_historical_position_base_rate.measurement: Tabulate winners by position, winning-team flag and era (1967-1990, 1991-2008, 2009-2026) from the official list; compute position shares with Beta shrinkage (prior weight 10 events) and incidence of losing-team and co-MVP outcomes; estimate drift with an era-weighted exponential decay (half-life 20 seasons) and use it as the prior intercept for the conditional-credit model.
raw_data: MVP list with position and team
nfl.sb_mvp_historical_position_base_rate.why: Base rate for the position and non-QB contracts, which have no season-stat process: it sets the prior that the game-level model refines.

nfl.sb_defender_highlight_hazard.label: Defender highlight hazard in a Super Bowl (sacks, takeaways, defensive TDs by player)
nfl.sb_defender_highlight_hazard.mechanism: Per-defender expected sacks, takeaways and defensive touchdowns in a game, weighted by pressure rate and the opponent's turnover tendency.
nfl.sb_defender_highlight_hazard.rationale: A defensive MVP needs an outlier game (several sacks, a pick-six or a strip-sack that changes the game); these are rare, high-variance events concentrated among a few edge rushers and ball-hawks and amplified in low-scoring wins. The opponent's offensive-line and quarterback sack and interception rates set the opportunity.
nfl.sb_defender_highlight_hazard.measurement: For each defender, estimate per-game sack and takeaway rates from pass-rush win rate or pressure rate and opponent pressure allowed, with a 3-season window shrunk to the position mean at 12 games of prior weight; add a defensive TD hazard per team-game from historical takeaway-to-TD conversion; compute P(2+ sacks or a defensive TD) per defender and combine with the winner's chance of a low-scoring win.
free_sources: Pass-rush win-rate provider (paid, ESPN or PFF)
nfl.sb_defender_highlight_hazard.why: Drives the defensive-player Super Bowl MVP variant, which is the only one of the four contracts decided mainly by defence.

nfl.season_sim_distribution.reason: Provides the finalist-pair distribution required for the team layer; needs the playoff structure to be modelled explicitly.

nfl.bracket_path.reason: Seed and path difficulty set finalist odds but do not choose the MVP; secondary to the simulation.

nfl.full_strength_rating_vs_season_avera.reason: The final is played with returned or lost starters, so a full-strength rating is the right team strength, not a season average.

nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.reason: Market-free rating is the base for the matchup probability and avoids price-derived inputs.

nfl.qb.reason: Starting QB status is the largest swing factor in position and non-QB variants.

nfl.injuries_pit.reason: Vintaged injury reports update availability for candidate players and the team layer.

nfl.qb_efficiency.reason: A regressed QB prior is useful for who posts the line but a single game is dominated by variance.

nfl.vote_outcome_model.reason: Vote-share model built for awards and a Top 100 list; a single-game panel needs recalibration but the structure applies.

nfl.award_voting_mechanics.reason: Voter pool, timing and tie rules are central here, though panel specifics for this award are not documented in the pack.

nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.reason: Credit splitting between a QB and top receiver or running back lowers each one's chance, a real effect in a single game.

nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.reason: Single-game ceiling tails give the chance of outlier lines, the highlights that drive voting.

nfl.td_rates.reason: Scoring rates by role project who scores in the game but are only weakly predictive of the vote.

nfl.script.reason: Script lattice decides which unit dominates; useful as a conditioning variable for credit allocation.

nfl.dst_td_hazard.reason: Defensive and special-teams TD hazard matters for defender and returner winners, which are rare.

nfl.pass_rush.reason: Pass-rush matchups raise sack opportunity for edge defenders but only enter through the defender hazard.

nfl.venue.reason: Neutral roof and surface only slightly shift run-pass balance; low weight.

nfl.ot_model.reason: Overtime rules add snaps and tail lines; the chance of overtime in a final is low, so a context input.

nfl.news.reason: Narrative and injury news in the two-week window move candidacy but the vote is on the game; keep with timestamps.

m.rules_text.reason: No rules text is available for any of the four series, so this input is the open settlement question rather than evidence.

m.settlement_truth.reason: The official announcement and position label settle the contract; no predictive value.

interactions.mechanism: P(player MVP) is the product of his team's win probability and his conditional credit share, so a star on the underdog can have lower probability than a supporting player on the favourite; credit shares are renormalised within the winner only.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose historical winners into team-win and within-team credit parts and test that the product reproduces observed MVP frequencies by team win probability bucket.

interactions.mechanism: In low-scoring, turnover-heavy wins a pick-six or multi-sack game becomes the standout line and defender MVP mass jumps; in shootouts it nearly vanishes, so the effect is a regime switch on the script.
interactions.how_to_test: Split past finals by total points and takeaway margin and compare the share of defensive MVPs across regimes.

interactions.mechanism: If the starting QB is injured, backup or the offence is run-first, the QB premium shrinks and mass moves to RB, WR and defence, so the position base rate is conditional on QB status.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition the position prior on QB availability and the winner's pass rate in the final and compare shares across subsets.

interactions.mechanism: A second strong line from a teammate dilutes the credit of the first; the combined probability of the pair rises less than the sum, so the response of one player's MVP chance to his own line is concave when a teammate also posts a big game.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the conditional logit with and without a teammate-competition term and test the sign and size of the penalty.

interactions.mechanism: Finalist odds are nonlinear in seed: the top seed gets the bye and a single-elimination path, so the probability of reaching the final is higher than the rating alone implies and mass concentrates on few teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated finalist frequencies with and without seed and bye effects against past playoff histories.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex above a threshold stat line (for example 3 or more TDs or 300+ passing yards)
nonlinearities.why: Voters respond to standout lines, so selection probability for a player rises sharply once his line crosses a visible threshold and is almost flat below it.

nonlinearities.shape: Softmax saturation: leading candidate share compresses as a second candidate rises
nonlinearities.why: Vote share across candidates is bounded and normalised; as one player's line grows the leader's share saturates, and split credit means the response is not linear in any one line.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic in rating margin with SD about 13 points
nonlinearities.why: Win probability is logistic in the margin, so a rating edge moves the team layer less near even matchups and the MVP chance is only modestly sensitive to rating differences.
